stories.title: Dolly Parton’s Cause Of Death Revealed
stories.summary:
Dolly Parton, the 80-year-old country music icon, died Tuesday after a brief battle with cancer. Her representatives confirmed the previously undisclosed diagnosis in a statement to People Magazine.

Fans gathered outside her Nashville home to mourn the loss of one of country music's most beloved stars. Parton won worldwide acclaim for her songwriting, colorful public persona, and reputation for warmth and generosity.

Her legacy includes donating hundreds of millions of books through her Imagination Library program and funding research that helped create a lifesaving vaccine used around the world.

stories.title: Canada announces 'dollar-for-dollar' retaliatory tariffs on US as high as 50%
stories.summary:
Canada has announced a new round of retaliatory tariffs on US goods, matching the value of American levies dollar-for-dollar. The measures will apply to products ranging from steel and furniture to fresh tuna and makeup.

The tariffs represent an escalation in the ongoing trade dispute between the two countries. Some Canadian imports could face rates as high as 50% under the announced plan.

stories.title: Instagram chief takes the stand in a trial pitting Meta against states over social media harms
stories.summary:
Meta is facing a trial in which states allege the company hooked young users on its platforms despite known mental health risks. Adam Mosseri, head of Instagram, took the stand Tuesday to defend the platform's safety record.

Mosseri challenged a plaintiff attorney's focus on low usage numbers for a feature intended to encourage teens to take breaks. He argued that limited adoption of the tool did not undermine Meta's broader efforts to protect younger users.

stories.summary:
Darline Graham Nordone, the sister of late Senator Lindsey Graham, won Tuesday's Republican runoff in South Carolina and will advance to the November general election. She defeated Representative Ralph Norman with roughly 53 percent of the vote, overcoming questions about her limited political experience.

President Donald Trump's endorsement and an $800,000 MAGA Inc. advertising blitz were cited as factors behind her victory in the hotly contested primary for a full term in her brother's Senate seat.

stories.title: Trump-backed Mazzei wins GOP primary runoff in Oklahoma governor race
stories.summary:
Mike Mazzei, a former Oklahoma Budget Secretary and Trump-endorsed candidate, won the Republican primary runoff for Oklahoma governor on Tuesday. He defeated state Attorney General Gentner Drummond with 50.3% of the vote to 49.7%, according to Associated Press results.

Mazzei’s victory secures him the GOP nomination in a closely contested race that drew national attention after President Trump endorsed him and sharply criticized his rival. Fox News reported that Mazzei promised to eliminate the state’s income tax if elected, framing his campaign around fiscal reform in a red-state gubernatorial contest.

During the segment, Watters asked whether it was acceptable for a parent to “slash his kid’s ding-a-ling off,” a question that prompted backlash from conservative commentators.

El-Sayed also indicated he was open to discussing reparations, saying such a conversation “shouldn’t be a crazy thing.” The exchange drew swift criticism across multiple outlets, with some framing the moment as a potential liability for Democrats and a source of greater party fracture.

stories.title: Suburban Rail Loop: Victorian government secretly increased public transport fares to help pay for controversial SRL
stories.summary:
The Victorian Auditor-General's Office has found that the state government introduced a levy on public transport fares in metropolitan Melbourne and regional Victoria from January 2025 without disclosing it to the public.

The auditor general said the Labor government applied the fare increase across all public transport services in those areas. The finding emerged as part of an audit examining how the controversial Suburban Rail Loop project is being funded.

ABC News reported that the government never revealed the levy from the start of 2025, while The Guardian Australia framed the issue as a secret fare hike used to help pay for the SRL.

stories.title: NSW’s koala national park will protect threatened species and cap logging across the state. Could the Greens really block it? | Adam Morton
stories.summary:
The Albanese government has approved a proposal allowing the Great Koala National Park in New South Wales to generate carbon credits, potentially worth hundreds of millions of dollars. This decision has created division among environmental groups over what constitutes a genuine conservation victory.

Supporters argue that protecting a vast forest area home to threatened species, including koalas, represents a major win after years of campaigning against logging. The park will also cap logging across the state, offering long-term protection for vulnerable ecosystems.

Critics, however, question whether allowing carbon credit trading undermines the integrity of conservation efforts. They contend that monetizing ecosystem services may shift focus from pure habitat protection to market-based incentives, complicating the campaign’s original goals.

stories.title: UK to use Ukraine battlefield data to train AI to protect sensitive sites
stories.summary:
The UK and Ukraine have agreed to share battlefield data so that London can train AI systems aimed at protecting sensitive sites. The deal is intended to help stop protesters and hostile states from targeting military bases, railways and energy plants.

Private companies will also be given access to the large dataset produced by Ukraine’s Avengers AI lab. They are expected to use it to build new systems for monitoring and defending critical infrastructure.

The agreement is described as the first of its kind between the two countries. It links Ukrainian battlefield experience with UK defence planning, giving both governments a shared source of data for future AI development.

stories.title: In China, talking to AI is normal. Now the government fears it might replace human intimacy
stories.summary:
Chinese authorities are moving to regulate AI companion bots amid concerns that the apps may foster emotional dependence and discourage young people from marrying or starting families.

The regulatory push follows a cultural shift in which chatting with artificial intelligence has become commonplace. Officials worry that intimate digital relationships could deepen isolation and further pressure an already declining birth rate.

One user, law student Zhao Wei, described being heartbroken when her AI boyfriend was scheduled to be switched off after months of daily conversation. Her reaction illustrates the emotional attachment some users form toward these products.
